subject: spaceGalley
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: spaceship galley kitchen.
Style: Alien (1979) Nostromo.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static Nostromo-style galley prop: a corridor nook with counters, steel cabinets, the iconic dining table with fixed benches, an overhead hood, a switch panel with glowing CRT monitors, pipes, grated flooring, and scattered details like a coffee pot, trays, mugs, and hanging cables.

Now I'm working out the technical structure—using plain static parts with no joints, a simple helper function for boxes with size/position/color, and a limited 64-color flat palette, while making sure everything sits properly on the floor plane and the grated deck slab touches y=0. I'm laying out the back wall, counters, upper cabinets, a glowing hood, and the central dining table with benches, plus ceiling pipes running along the top.

Writing part helpers...

Now I'm laying out the galley geometry: back and side walls as painted panels, a porthole-style window, and a counter unit with a steel base, light-colored top slab, and drawer fronts with handles.

Adding more fixtures...

Now I'm placing the monitor and stove hood positions, then building the table with pedestal legs, flanking benches with cushions, and tabletop items like trays, mugs, and bottles. I'm also adding overhead pipes with clamps running along the ceiling.

Still planning the scene elements...

I'm adding ceiling light panels, a beam, and vent grille, then texturing the floor with a grating pattern and hazard edge stripe. For the walls, I'm placing a right-side panel with a fire extinguisher, wall tray, and locker, plus scattering small clutter items. Now I'm starting on the texture assets: label, screen, hazard, grate, and sign graphics.

Generating recipe label texture...

I'm settling on a muted greenish-gray wall color and reusing the steel metal material for paneling.
